name: Technodrome AI Content Assistant
author: technodrome

sections.description:
Technodrome AI Content Assistant is a powerful WordPress plugin that enables you to generate high-quality AI-powered content using curated article-first AI providers including OpenAI (GPT), Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini), DeepSeek, Cohere, Together AI, and Mistral AI.

Key Features

  • Curated AI Providers: Choose from a smaller article-first provider lineup with carefully shortlisted text models
  • Profile System: Save and manage multiple content generation profiles with custom settings
  • Layout Templates: 6 professional templates with drag-and-drop builder for custom layouts
  • Content Rules: Create custom rules for headings, guidelines, and writing style
  • 40+ Languages: Generate content in any language with native-quality output
  • Article-Only Model Catalog: Avoid confusing image, audio, reasoning-only, deprecated, and code-first model clutter
  • AutoSave Revolution: Automatic profile saving and content history

NEW in v4.0.0 – AI + Video Context Generation

  • AI + Video URL Context (PREMIUM): Generate articles from single video URLs (YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok)
  • AI + Video Channel Context (PREMIUM): Generate articles from entire video channels
  • Video Slot Transformation: Smart slot locking based on selected generation mode
  • Compact Notification: Clear UI feedback when video context mode is active

License

This plugin is licensed under GPL v2 or later. See LICENSE file for details.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/technodrome-ai-content-assistant directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Configure your AI provider API keys in the plugin settings.
  4. Start generating AI content!
sections.faq:
Do I need an API key?

Yes, you need an API key from your chosen AI provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.).

Is this plugin free?

The core plugin is free. Video URL and Video Channel Context modes require a PREMIUM license.

Which AI providers are supported?

OpenAI (GPT), Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini), DeepSeek, Cohere, Together AI, and Mistral AI.
sections.changelog:
5.0.0 (2026-08-09)

  • NEW – Images in your articles: new Auto mode lets the same AI model that writes the article also draw the picture, in a single call. OpenAI uses the Responses API image_generation tool; Google Gemini uses native image output (responseModalities). Gemini is now an image-capable provider – previously selecting it disabled image generation entirely.
  • NEW – Resolution and Quality controls: pick 1024×1024 / 1792×1024 / 1024×1792 / 1280×720 / 720×1280, plus a separate Quality setting (Low / Standard / High) that maps to the provider’s own quality scale. Also a 2-row Image Description box and a Style picker.
  • FIX – Retired default model: dall-e-3 was retired by OpenAI on 2026-03-04 but was still the default image model, so image generation failed by default. Replaced with GPT Image 2; old profiles holding dall-e-3 are transparently remapped instead of erroring.
  • CHANGED – UI: AI Image Generation moved out of the Generate tab into the Content Rules tab (right column, above Web Sources) as a highlighted, FREE section with light and dark mode styling. The AI Provider panel is reordered into its logical setup sequence: 1. AI Provider – 2. API Key – 3. AI Model.
  • FIX – Auto mode failed with an error naming the old image model: the main model was read from the wrong array key so Auto always used a hardcoded fallback, and the resolution list offered sizes the image models reject. Resolutions are now clamped to what the chosen model supports, and Auto falls back to gpt-image-2 when the chat model returns no image (the GPT-5.6 Luna/Terra/Sol variants do not drive the image tool).
  • CHANGED – Switch and settings split by purpose: the plain YES/NO switch sits in the Generate tab, row 3 next to AI Model (refresh | AI Model | switch | AI IMAGE); the settings stay in Content Rules and are dimmed, not hidden, while the switch is off. A new refresh button reloads the provider’s model list without a page reload.
  • CHANGED – Capability detection: image support is now decided per provider instead of a hardcoded per-model whitelist that went stale with every new model release.

4.9.1 (2026-08-02)

  • CRITICAL FIX: Removed UTF-8 BOM from 10 PHP files (including the main plugin file) that emitted output on line 1 and caused “Cannot modify header information – headers already sent”, breaking wp-login.php and wp-admin while the plugin was active.
  • FIX: Removed trailing ?> close tags from 4 files; class-profile-manager.php was emitting 6 bytes of trailing whitespace on every request.
  • HARDENING: ABSPATH direct-access guard moved to the top of the main plugin file.
  • CLEANUP: Removed 4 empty dead class files that were loaded on every request via require_once.

4.9.0 (2026-07-11)

  • PROVIDER UPDATE: Model catalog and defaults aligned with Joomla 4.9.0, including GPT-5.6, Claude 5, and Gemini 3.5 Flash defaults.
  • CONNECTIVITY: Added central HTTP transport with SSL verification and targeted IPv4 retry for hosting-level traffic/network failures.
  • SECURITY: Photo uploads now use server-side MIME/image validation and server-selected extensions.
  • FIX: Restored missing Photo Manager implementation and improved OpenAI image generation for URL/base64 responses.
